concept.name: Wyckoff distribution
concept.definition: The phase of the Wyckoff price cycle in which large interests sell (or short) a sizeable position inside a trading range after an uptrend, exhausting demand and building the 'cause' for a later markdown. It is a hypothesized topping structure, not a proven signal that prices must fall.
concept.intuition: The insiders quietly unload their holdings onto enthusiastic late buyers; the price stops rising because every rally meets a wall of supply.
concept.mechanics: A distribution trading range typically shows preliminary supply and a buying climax, an automatic reaction, and secondary tests (Phase A); a cause-building stretch where institutions are net sellers (Phase B); a test of remaining demand such as an upthrust or UTAD (Phase C); signs of weakness with lower highs and last points of supply (Phase D); and a breakdown as supply takes control (Phase E).
concept.failure_modes: Apparent distribution can be re-accumulation instead, in which case the range breaks out upward; climactic buying can resume rather than top, and in strong bull markets many labeled 'distribution' ranges simply continue higher.
concept.misconceptions: A distribution range does not require an upthrust-after-distribution, and the pattern is often recognizable only in its second half; calling a top in real time is one of the framework's most error-prone applications.
concept.example: After a long rally, a stock churns sideways for seven months with volume heavier on down days; a brief pop above the range high fails (UTAD), and a later break of range support on wide spreads marks the start of markdown.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
